core_obligations: Detect a finite-dimensional twisted harmonic spinor from the nonvanishing Rosenberg index after Ricci-flat splitting.
Untwist the parallel spinor on the universal cover.
Construct a finite torus cover with trivialized pullback spin structure and descend the parallel-spinor conclusion.
difficulty_reason: The implication from nonnegative scalar curvature to a finite cover with a parallel spinor combines higher-index spectral detection for virtually abelian fundamental groups, spinor untwisting, and a finite-cover spin-structure construction. This links analytic higher index data to geometric parallel spinors and is beyond routine scalar-curvature manipulation.

dedup.scope: Root complete DOI+arxiv2411.03882 lookup found no same-work records. Focused Rosenberg-index neighbor1652 (SIGMA2020.127, Theorem1.4) concerns scalar-curvature negative upper bounds forced by a pi1-injective hypersurface with nonzero index; this task concerns closed Ricci-flat spin manifolds and equivalent parallel-spinor/finite-cover/nonnegative-scalar-curvature conditions, with distinct assumptions and output.

compared.difference: Hypersurface-induced width/scalar-curvature obstruction versus closed-manifold Ricci-flatness and existence of parallel spinors on finite covers.
